title: Sales/CS Enterprise Request Aggregation & Initial Scoping Playbook
creator: Anika Rao
body:
Summary:
This ticket captures a repeatable playbook for receiving, aggregating, and doing an initial scoping pass on enterprise feature requests that originate from Sales and Customer Success (non-bug asks). The goal is to reduce friction for Sales/CS, create a consistent scoring rubric that Product and Eng can use for prioritization, and produce a one-page scoping artifact per request that supports go/no-go decisions and pricing conversations.

Motivation & context:
- We currently see long-lived back-and-forths between Sales/CS and Product for enterprise asks; time to first response is inconsistent and senior AE cycles are overloaded.
- Enterprise customers often bundle functional requests with security/compliance asks that materially change effort. Early triage on compliance and infra requirements avoids waste.
- A consistent intake surface will enable better capacity planning for Dedicated & Private offerings and faster commercial decisions.

Goals for the playbook:
1) Provide a single intake form for AE/CS that auto-populates the intake queue.
2) Define a lightweight scoring rubric (impact, revenue, effort, risk) used across PM/Eng/Legal.
3) Create a 1-page scoping template that includes acceptance criteria, rough engineering sizes, security flags, and recommended pricing uplift.
4) Set SLAs for initial triage (48h) and preliminary scoping (10 business days).

Stakeholders:
- Sales: Heather Kim (lead AE contributor)
- Customer Success: Marco Jimenez (CS Enterprise)
- Product: Anika Rao (owner), Ethan Park (assignee)
- Eng: Priya Nair (runtime), Luis Chen (infra)
- Design: Marie Dubois (input on intake UX)
- Legal/Security: Omar Wallace (compliance review)

Proposed intake flow (high level):
1) AE/CS submits intake form (Confluence + Google Form backstop) with required fields below.
2) Intake queue created in Linear under project "enterprise-intake-framework". Triage PM (rotating) assigns to PM owner.
3) PM does initial triage within 48 hours: verifies ask, identifies primary use-case, flags security/compliance items, estimates revenue/opportunity, and scores request.
4) If score passes threshold, PM creates a 1-page scoping artifact and requests Eng/Design feedback (target 10 business days).
5) Commercial team (Sales Ops) receives cost estimate and pricing uplift recommendation.

Minimum required intake fields (for the form):
- Company name, ARR, contract size, and expected launch date
- Short problem statement (1-2 sentences), example prompts / sample data
- Why Redwood? (vendor constraints, hosting needs)
- Desired SLA/latency/capacity targets
- Security/regulatory constraints (e.g., HIPAA, ISO, FedRAMP)
- Preferred deployment: Hosted / Dedicated / Private
- Rough adoption: pilots / 1 team / org-wide

Scoring rubric (0-5 each, threshold: >=12 / max 20):
- Customer impact (0 none - 5 strategic customer / reference)
- Revenue opportunity (0 none - 5 multi-year strategic)
- Engineering effort (0 trivial - 5 ~6+ sprints) [inverse scored: high effort = lower points]
- Compliance/operational risk (0 low - 5 high) [inverse scored]

Sample 1-page scoping template (to be auto-generated from intake):
- Title / Short summary
- Core acceptance criteria (3 bullets)
- Assumptions & out-of-scope
- Proposed solution sketch (1 paragraph)
- Rough eng size (T-shirt + points) and primary owners
- Security flags and next steps for legal review
- Estimated timeline and gating milestones
- Recommended commercial approach (pilot/POC + uplift %)

Integration & artifacts:
- Intake form should create a Confluence page and link back to Linear ticket; Confluence template: /confluence/redwood/enterprise-intake-template
- Link to example pricing calculator: https://docs.redwood.ai/pricing/pricing-calculator (placeholder)
- Engineering kickoff checklist (ENG-2890) will be referenced in the scoping template.

Decision trade-offs considered:
- Fast triage vs. completeness: we bias to a lightweight first pass that can defer detailed security scoping until scoring passes.
- Automated scoring vs. human review: start with manual scoring to calibrate; evaluate ML-assisted routing in Q3 2026.
- Hosted feature parity vs. Dedicated-only: mandate deployment target on intake to avoid surprises.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- Intake form published (Confluence + Google Form) and linked from Sales playbook.
- Linear queue automation configured to create PM tickets for new submissions.
- Scoring rubric documented and two calibration sessions completed with Sales & Eng.
- One-page scoping template implemented in Confluence and used for at least 3 real customer asks in pilot.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Under-scoring security issues early -> Mitigation: introduce mandatory security flag and 24h legal acknowledgement for flagged requests.
- Risk: Sales friction -> Mitigation: keep form <10 fields and provide AE cheat-sheet + Slack macro.

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Draft intake form fields (Anika) — due 2026-02-20 (done).
- Build Linear automation with Sales Ops (Ethan / Grace) — in progress, ETA 2026-03-12.
- Hold calibration workshop with Eng & Legal — scheduled 2026-03-05 (notes linked below).
- Pilot with 3 live requests from Sales (target start 2026-03-15).
